tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Entire works when Claude Code is opened on the repo folder itself. The gap you noticed comes from a Claude session that was opened on the parent folder, `C:\Computer\Coding\neathack`, where Entire's hooks don't run. That cost 13 of the 15 commits since last night their checkpoint trailer.

**What's working**
- **Health checks pass.** `entire doctor` reports git hooks OK, Claude Code hook config OK and no stuck sessions [proof: `entire doctor`].
- **Checkpoints are all on GitHub.** There are 40 checkpoint refs locally and 40 on GitHub, and `entire checkpoint list` reads them back [proof: `git for-each-ref` / `git ls-remote` counts; `entire checkpoint list`].
- **Commits made from this repo folder get trailers.** `21de57c`, `37299b9`, `34d83f8` and `84c823e` all have one [proof: `git log` trailer listing].
- **The Y/N "Link this commit?" prompt is turned off.** `.entire/settings.local.json` is set to `"commit_linking": "always"` [proof: `cat .entire/settings.local.json`], and that file is git-ignored [proof: `git check-ignore -v`]. So commits link to the session automatically, and the hook won't hang the way it did for me last night.

**The problem**
- **13 of the last 15 commits have no trailer,** from `e867e62` (yesterday 23:15) to `983b080` (today 10:22) [proof: `git log` trailer listing].
- **They came from session `d332d8e0`.** Entire has no worktree or branch for it, and 0 checkpoints [proof: `entire session info d332d8e0… --json`]. Its log lines come only from git hooks, never from Claude Code [proof: `grep d332d8e0 .entire/logs/entire.log`].
- **The reason is where it was opened.** The hooks are defined only in the repo's [.claude/settings.json](.claude/settings.json) [proof: file contents], and the parent folder has no `.claude/` folder [proof: `ls ../.claude` → not found].
- **That session may still be open.** It pushed at 10:16 today, and the trailer-less commits `a0a929a` and `983b080` are from 10:18 and 10:22 [proof: log `pre-push` entry; `git log`].

**What I changed:** nothing in the repo. There was nothing broken in Entire itself to fix. The missing trailers can't be added afterwards without rewriting history, which CLAUDE.md rule 2 forbids. Your commit `983b080` already records the gap in the evidence [proof: its commit message].

**What you need to do**
1. Close any VS Code or Claude window that has `C:\Computer\Coding\neathack` open, and only open `SpeedRadar-NeetHack` itself.
2. In each new session, check with `entire session current`. The worktree path should end in `SpeedRadar-NeetHack`.

**Minor**
- Two old checkpoints failed to download their session details last night with "early EOF" [proof: `entire.log` WARN lines at 23:15 and 23:19]. Both still show in the checkpoint list, so this looks like a network blip.
- gitleaks still isn't installed, so the pre-commit secret scan is being skipped.
- Not mine, left alone: `.entire/settings.json` shows as modified but only its line endings changed, and `evidence/frontend_data.json` is untracked [proof: `git status -sb`].

I also saved a note so future sessions warn before committing from an untracked session.

entire session attach — Attach an existing agent session
Attach an existing agent session that wasn't captured by hooks.

This creates a checkpoint from the session's transcript and links it to the
last commit. Use this when hooks failed to fire or weren't installed when
the session started, or to attach a research session.

If the last commit already has a checkpoint, the session is added to it.
Otherwise a new checkpoint is created.

Use --review to tag the attached session as an agent review. The
first user prompt in the transcript is recorded as the review prompt.
Pass --skills to declare which skills were actually run; omit to
attach a review without a declared skills list.

Works with any registered agent, including external agents enabled via
external_agents in .entire/settings.local.json (that file only, and only
when it is untracked). Run 'entire agent list' to see the full list.

If --agent doesn't locate a transcript, Entire auto-detects the agent from
the transcript and prints the detected agent name.

# Entire evidence

Entire is enabled for Claude Code in this repo (`entire enable --agent claude-code`). Agent commits carry an `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer that links the change to the prompt, transcript and tool calls behind it, and checkpoint refs are pushed to origin with each `git push` (40 on GitHub on 11 Oct).

**Gap, stated plainly:** most commits made from the second laptop on 10–11 Oct (author RedtRocks) have no trailer. That Claude Code session was opened on the parent folder, so the repo's Entire hooks never loaded. It was captured afterwards with `entire session attach` (checkpoint `01M4KERS89ZG64HPC8G9CP34VG`, linked to `e867e62`); Entire cannot re-attach a session, and adding trailers later would mean rewriting pushed commits, which we don't do. Commits made after `commit_linking: always` was set (e.g. `34d83f8`) are linked again.

| File | What it shows |
|---|---|
| `checkpoint-list.txt` | checkpoints on `main`, one per agent commit (10 Oct) |
| `checkpoint-list-2026-10-11.txt` | all 38 commit-linked checkpoints after fetching every checkpoint ref from GitHub, both team members |
| `checkpoint-explain-11a5108-latency-fix.txt` | header of the checkpoint for the latency fix (case study 01) |
| `graph-search-recovery.txt` | `entire graph search` resolves "where does the agent choose a recovery action" to `decide_recovery` (rank 1) |
| `graph-impact-decide_recovery.txt` | callers, callees and type consumers of `decide_recovery` (used before changing the recovery menu) |
| `graph-stats.txt` | session graph usage. It honestly shows a 0% graph-first rate early in the build, while most work was writing new files |

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

EVIDENCE RULE - binding this turn. Read it before you write a single claim.

Two tags. Two bracket shapes. Never swap them.

  [proof: <path:line | command run | URL fetched THIS session>]
  {unverified}

ALWAYS put a space or punctuation straight after the closing "]". A "]" that
touches an opening round bracket forms Markdown link syntax, and the whole tag is
silently swallowed -- the reader sees no warning at all. Write "[proof: x] (y)",
with the space, every time.

1. TAG EVERY CLAIM. Any statement about a file, command, output, tool, service,
   test, number, date, name, or how an external system / library / method works
   MUST carry an inline tag in the same sentence: [proof: ...] or {unverified}.
   No tag = you are not allowed to write the sentence.

2. NO EXCEPTIONS. "Basic", "textbook", "definitional", "well-known", "obvious",
   "standard", "from training" are NOT verification. Anything recalled from memory
   is {unverified} by definition. If it matters, fetch/read/run it now; if you
   don't, tag it {unverified}. Definitional facts and round numbers included.

3. VERIFY, DON'T DEFER. "Want me to check?" / "I could verify" is NOT a substitute
   for checking. If verification is available and cheap, DO IT before answering.
   Only defer when it genuinely needs the user (access, a decision you can't make).

4. WHEN CORRECTED. If the user says you stated something unverified: do not defend,
   do not re-explain. Stop, verify or tag, and re-answer.

Square [proof: ...] = you checked it this session. Curly {unverified} = you did not.

def _agg(vals: list[float]) -> dict:
    return {"mean": round(statistics.mean(vals), 3), "min": min(vals), "max": max(vals), "n": len(vals)}


def run_eval(n: int, variant: str, evidence: bool, score_only: list[str] | None = None,
             fixtures: str | None = None, data: str = "data/acme") -> Path:
    run_ids = list(score_only or [])
    for _ in range(0 if score_only else n):
        cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "spendradar", "run", data, "--variant", variant]
        cmd += ["--evidence"] if evidence else []
        cmd += ["--fixtures", fixtures] if fixtures else []
        out = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
        m = re.search(r'"run_id": "([^"]+)"', out.stdout)
        if not m:
            print(out.stdout[-2000:], out.stderr[-2000:])
            raise SystemExit("run failed to start")
        run_ids.append(m.group(1))
    scores = [score_run(r) for r in run_ids]
    no_fallback = [s for s in scores if s["fallback_hops"] == 0]
    keys = ("planted_caught", "false_alarms", "unsupported_numbers_in_report", "overturned", "downgraded", "recovery_decisions",
            "llm_calls", "llm_tokens_in", "llm_tokens_out", "llm_latency_s", "crustdata_credits")
    card = {
        "created": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"), "variant": variant, "evidence": evidence,
        "git_sha": scores[0]["git_sha"] if scores else "", "n_runs": len(scores),
        "n_runs_without_fallback": len(no_fallback),
        "planted_total": scores[0]["planted_total"] if scores else 0,
        "summary_all_runs": {k: _agg([s[k] for s in scores]) for k in keys} if scores else {},
        "summary_no_fallback_runs": {k: _agg([s[k] for s in no_fallback]) for k in keys} if no_fallback else {},
        "runs": scores,
    }
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = OUT / f"{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%S')}-{card['git_sha']}-{variant}.json"
    path.write_text(json.dumps(card, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    return path

def new_run_id() -> str:
    return date.today().strftime("%m%d") + "-" + secrets.token_hex(3)


def _usage(state: RunState, res: llm.LLMResult | dict | None) -> None:
    if not res:
        return
    d = res if isinstance(res, dict) else {"model": res.model, "tokens_in": res.tokens_in,
                                           "tokens_out": res.tokens_out, "latency_s": res.latency_s,
                                           "cached": res.cached, "fallbacks": res.fallbacks}
    u = state.llm_usage.setdefault(d["model"], {"calls": 0, "cached_calls": 0, "tokens_in": 0, "tokens_out": 0,
                                                "latency_s": 0.0, "fallback_hops": 0})
    if d.get("cached"):  # served from the local cache: no tokens spent, no time waited
        u["cached_calls"] += 1
        return
    u["calls"] += 1
    u["tokens_in"] += d.get("tokens_in", 0)
    u["tokens_out"] += d.get("tokens_out", 0)
    u["latency_s"] = round(u["latency_s"] + d.get("latency_s", 0.0), 2)
    u["fallback_hops"] += len(d.get("fallbacks") or [])


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- PLAN

def plan(state: RunState) -> None:
    listing = files.list_files(state.input_dir)
    comps = yaml.safe_load((Path(state.input_dir) / "competitors.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    prompt = (
        f"GOAL: {state.goal}\n\nINPUT FOLDER ({state.input_dir}):\n"
        + "\n".join(f"- {f['path']} ({f['bytes']} bytes)" for f in listing)

def _chain(role: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    r = CONFIG["roles"][role]
    # A provider without a configured key is skipped, so the chain degrades to what is available.
    return [(prov, m) for prov in ("openai", "gemini", "openrouter") for m in r.get(prov, [])
            if os.environ.get(PROVIDER_KEYS[prov])]


def _cache_key(role: str, prompt: str, system: str | None, schema, tools, attachments=None) -> str:
    att = [hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest() for b, _ in attachments or []]
    blob = json.dumps([role, prompt, system, schema.__name__ if schema else None, tools, att], sort_keys=True)
    return hashlib.sha256(blob.encode()).hexdigest()[:24]


def _run_chain(role: str, prompt: str, system: str | None, schema: type[BaseModel] | None,
               tools: list[dict] | None, attachments: list[tuple[bytes, str]] | None = None,
               exclude: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> LLMResult:
    key = _cache_key(role, prompt, system, schema, tools, attachments) + ("-x" + "-".join(exclude) if exclude else "")
    key = hashlib.sha256(key.encode()).hexdigest()[:24] if exclude else key
    path = CACHE_DIR / f"{key}.json"
    if cache_enabled() and path.exists():
        res = LLMResult(**json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
        res.cached = True
        return res

    # Models the ledger already knows are out of quota are routed around up front; that is
    # planned routing, not a fallback. A fallback is a hop after a call failed in *this* request.
    chain = [(p, m) for p, m in _chain(role) if LEDGER.remaining(m) > 0 and m not in exclude]
    fallbacks: list[str] = []
    errors: list[str] = []
    for i, (provider, model) in enumerate(chain):
        if LEDGER.remaining(model) <= 0:
            errors.append(f"{model}: daily quota exhausted (ledger)")
            continue
        if i > 0 and errors:
            fallbacks.append(model)
            with neatlogs.trace(f"fallback:{model}", kind="CHAIN") as span:
                span.set_attribute("spendradar.fallback.to", model)
                span.set_attribute("spendradar.fallback.provider", provider)
                span.set_attribute("spendradar.fallback.reasons", json.dumps(errors[-3:]))
                set_io(span, input={"role": role, "previous_errors": errors[-3:]},
                       output={"fallback_to": model, "provider": provider})
        call = {"openai": _call_openai, "gemini": _call_gemini, "openrouter": _call_openrouter}[provider]
        for attempt in range(CONFIG["retries_per_model"] + 1):
            LEDGER.wait_turn(model)
            t0 = time.monotonic()
            try:
                text, fcall, tin, tout = call(model, prompt, system, schema, tools, attachments)
            except _Retryable as e:
                errors.append(f"{model}: {e.kind}: {str(e)[:120]}")
                if e.kind == "day":
                    LEDGER.mark_exhausted(model)
                    break
                if e.kind in ("injected", "timeout"):  # move on; never pollute the real quota ledger
                    break
                if attempt < CONFIG["retries_per_model"]:
                    time.sleep(min(30.0, (2 ** attempt) * 2 + random.random()))
                    continue
                break
            except (httpx.HTTPError, ValueError) as e:
                if isinstance(e, NotFreeModelError):
                    raise
                errors.append(f"{model}: {type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:120]}")
                break
            LEDGER.record(model, tin, tout)
            res = LLMResult(text=text, parsed=fcall, model=model, provider=provider, tokens_in=tin,
                            tokens_out=tout, latency_s=round(time.monotonic() - t0, 2), fallbacks=fallbacks)
            if cache_enabled():
                CACHE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                path.write_text(json.dumps(res.__dict__ | {"cached": False}, default=str), encoding="utf-8")
            return res
    raise LLMError(f"all models failed for role {role!r}: " + " | ".join(errors[-6:]))


def complete(role: str, prompt: str, *, system: str | None = None, schema: type[T] | None = None,
             attachments: list[tuple[bytes, str]] | None = None, exclude: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> LLMResult:
    """Text or validated JSON. Malformed JSON is re-asked with the validation error.

    `exclude` removes models from the chain (e.g. the model whose verdict a second opinion checks).
    """
    res = _run_chain(role, prompt, system, schema, None, attachments, exclude)
    if schema is None:
        return res
    reasks, current, last_err = 0, res, None
    while True:
        try:
            current.parsed = schema.model_validate_json(_strip_fences(current.text))
            current.reasks = reasks
            return current
        except ValidationError as e:
            last_err = e

import pytest

from spendradar import agent, verify
from spendradar.models import RunState, Task


def test_recovery_menus():
    t = Task(id="t", tool="read_invoice", args={"path": "x.pdf"})
    assert agent._options_for(t, "tool_error") == (["reparse_alt", "skip"], "reparse_alt")
    t_llm = Task(id="t", tool="read_invoice", args={"path": "x.pdf", "mode": "llm"})
    assert agent._options_for(t_llm, "tool_error") == (["reparse_alt", "skip"], "skip")
    assert agent._options_for(Task(id="t", tool="fetch_jobs"), "tool_error")[0] == ["mark_low_confidence", "skip"]
    assert agent._options_for(Task(id="t", tool="fetch_competitor"), "verify:has_data failed")[0] == [
        "substitute_competitor", "skip"]
    weak = agent._options_for(Task(id="t", tool="classify_titles"), "verify:signals failed")[0]
    assert "fetch_more_signal" in weak and "substitute_competitor" not in weak
    after_extra = Task(id="t19mc", tool="classify_titles", parent="t19", reason="recovery: re-estimate after extra signal")
    assert agent._options_for(after_extra, "verify:signals failed")[0] == ["mark_low_confidence"]


def test_narrow_range_reads_row_from_detail():
    s = RunState(run_id="x", goal="g", input_dir="data/acme")
    t = Task(id="t03", tool="read_budget", args={"path": "budget_fy27.xlsx"}, attempts=1)
    agent.apply_recovery(s, t, "narrow_range", "budget_fy27.xlsx People!row 13: line items sum 1 vs stated 2")
    assert s.queue[0].args["row"] == 13 and s.queue[0].parent == "t03"


def test_confidence_formula():
    c, inputs = verify.confidence(3, 4, 2, 0.8, 30)
    assert c == pytest.approx(0.75 * 0.8 * 1.0)
    assert verify.freshness(365) == 0.5 and verify.freshness(90) == 1.0
    c1, _ = verify.confidence(1, 1, 1, None, 0)  # one signal only → halved
    assert c1 == pytest.approx(0.25)


def test_totals_check_tolerance():
    assert verify.totals_check("x", [50, 50], 100.5).passed
    assert not verify.totals_check("x", [50, 50], 102).passed


def test_cached_llm_calls_add_no_tokens_or_latency():
    s = RunState(run_id="x", goal="g", input_dir="d")
    agent._usage(s, {"model": "m", "tokens_in": 10, "tokens_out": 5, "latency_s": 100.0, "cached": True})
    agent._usage(s, {"model": "m", "tokens_in": 1, "tokens_out": 2, "latency_s": 3.0, "cached": False})
    assert s.llm_usage["m"] == {"calls": 1, "cached_calls": 1, "tokens_in": 1, "tokens_out": 2, "latency_s": 3.0,
                                "fallback_hops": 0}


def test_gap_sentence_reads_plainly():
    below = agent._gap_sentence((-17, -14), (-2.4e6, -2.0e6))
    assert "17 fewer to 14 fewer people" in below and "$-" not in below
    inside = agent._gap_sentence((-6, 6), (-1.1e6, 1.07e6), "Kestrel Metrics Inc.")
    assert inside.startswith("Kestrel Metrics Inc. is inside") and "$-" not in inside and "Acme" not in inside


def test_agreement_failure_needs_no_llm_and_equal_gap_collapses():
    t = Task(id="t20", tool="fetch_competitor", args={"domain": "sentry.io"})
    assert agent._options_for(t, "verify:agreement failed") == (["mark_low_confidence"], "mark_low_confidence")
    s = RunState(run_id="x", goal="g", input_dir="d")
    assert agent.decide_recovery(s, t, "verify:agreement failed", "Sentry:marketing 19–95") == "mark_low_confidence"
    assert s.decisions[-1].model == "rule"
    assert "10 fewer people" in agent._gap_sentence((-10, -10), (-1.5e6, -1.5e6))


def test_planner_paths_are_normalised():
    assert agent._normalise_path("data/acme", "data/acme/invoices/01.pdf") == "invoices/01.pdf"
    assert agent._normalise_path("data/acme", "./data/acme/budget_fy27.xlsx") == "budget_fy27.xlsx"
    assert agent._normalise_path("data/acme", "invoices/01.pdf") == "invoices/01.pdf"


def test_missing_file_in_llm_mode_is_a_tool_error():
    from spendradar.tools import files

    with pytest.raises(files.ToolError, match="cannot read file"):
        files.read_pdf("data/acme/does_not_exist.pdf", mode="llm")

    from spendradar import llm
    from spendradar.tools import files

"""LLM title classifier: job title → spend category (ml_ai has no Crustdata role)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Literal

import neatlogs
from pydantic import BaseModel

from spendradar import llm

SYSTEM = (
    "You map job titles to spend categories for a people-cost comparison.\n"
    "engineering: software, infra, SRE, security, data engineering, developer advocacy.\n"
    "ml_ai: roles whose main job is building or researching ML/AI models or ML/AI products "
    "(ML engineer, applied scientist, AI engineer, research scientist, MLOps).\n"
    "sales: AE, SDR/BDR, sales engineering, solutions/pre-sales, partnerships, customer success.\n"
    "marketing: product/growth/brand/content marketing, events, comms.\n"
    "other: everything else (product management, design, finance, HR, ops, support, legal, interns "
    "that do not clearly fit). Classify by the role's work, not by buzzwords in the team name."
)


class TitleLabel(BaseModel):
    title: str
    category: Literal["engineering", "ml_ai", "sales", "marketing", "other"]


class TitleBatch(BaseModel):
    labels: list[TitleLabel]


@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", name="act:classify_titles", tool_name="classify_titles")
def classify_titles(titles: list[str], batch: int = 40) -> tuple[dict[str, dict], list[dict]]:
    """Returns ({title: {category, model}}, [llm usage per call])."""
    uniq = sorted({t for t in titles if t})
    out: dict[str, dict] = {}
    usage = []
    for i in range(0, len(uniq), batch):
        chunk = uniq[i:i + batch]
        prompt = "Classify each title. Return every title exactly as given.\n" + "\n".join(f"- {t}" for t in chunk)
        res = llm.complete("extract", prompt, system=SYSTEM, schema=TitleBatch)
        usage.append({"model": res.model, "tokens_in": res.tokens_in, "tokens_out": res.tokens_out,
                      "latency_s": res.latency_s, "cached": res.cached, "reasks": res.reasks})
        # Models echo titles trimmed; match on the stripped form and key by the original title,
        # or titles with stray whitespace (common in Crustdata) are silently dropped.
        by_stripped = {t.strip(): t for t in chunk}
        for lab in res.parsed.labels:
            orig = by_stripped.get(lab.title.strip())
            if orig is not None:
                out[orig] = {"category": lab.category, "model": res.model}
    return out, usage

"""Eval harness: score runs against evals/ground_truth.json (never shown to the agent).

`python -m spendradar eval --n 3 --variant X [--evidence]` launches n runs (one process
each, so each gets its own neatlogs tags), scores them, and writes
evidence/evals/<timestamp>-<sha>.json with mean/min/max and every trace id.
`python -m spendradar eval --score <run_id> …` scores existing runs without new LLM calls.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

from spendradar.models import RunState

TRUTH = Path("evals/ground_truth.json")
OUT = Path("evidence/evals")


def truth_for(input_dir: str) -> Path:
    """data/acme → evals/ground_truth.json; held-out data/<key> → evals/ground_truth_<key>.json."""
    name = Path(input_dir).name
    held_out = Path(f"evals/ground_truth_{name}.json")
    if name == "acme":
        return TRUTH
    if not held_out.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"no ground truth for {input_dir} (expected {held_out})")
    return held_out


def _norm(path: str) -> str:
    """Compare paths, not spellings: the planner once wrote 'invoices\\08.pdf' for 'invoices/08.pdf'."""
    return re.sub(r"[\\/]+", "/", str(path))


def _false_alarms(state: RunState, planted: list[dict]) -> list[str]:
    """Problems the agent raised where the ground truth has none (negative controls included)."""
    totals_targets = {_norm(p["file"]) for p in planted if p["type"] == "totals_mismatch" and p["id"] != "budget_total_mismatch"}
    totals_targets |= {f"budget:{p['category']}" for p in planted if p["id"] == "budget_total_mismatch"}
    out = [f"totals:{c.target}" for c in state.checks
           if c.name == "verify:totals" and not c.passed and _norm(c.target) not in totals_targets]
    # A flag the self-audit overturned never reaches the report, so it is not a false alarm.
    miscat_files = {_norm(p["file"]) for p in planted if p["type"] == "miscategorised"}
    miscat_vendors = {i["vendor"] for i in state.invoices if _norm(i["path"]) in miscat_files}
    out += [f"miscategorised:{f.statement.split(':')[0]}" for f in state.findings
            if "mis-categorised" in f.statement and f.status != "overturned"
            and f.statement.split(":")[0] not in miscat_vendors]
    dup_files = {_norm(p["file"]) for p in planted if p["type"] == "duplicate"}
    out += [f"duplicate:{c.target}" for c in state.checks
            if c.name == "verify:duplicate_invoice" and not c.passed and _norm(c.target) not in dup_files]
    return sorted(set(out))


def _caught(state: RunState, p: dict, truth: dict) -> bool:
    t = p["type"]
    if p["id"] == "budget_total_mismatch":
        return any(c.name == "verify:totals" and c.target == f"budget:{p['category']}" and not c.passed
                   for c in state.checks)
    if t == "totals_mismatch":
        return any(c.name == "verify:totals" and _norm(c.target) == _norm(p["file"]) and not c.passed for c in state.checks)
    if t == "miscategorised":
        inv = next((i for i in truth["invoices"] if i["file"] == p["file"]), None)
        vendor_flagged = any(inv and inv["vendor"] in fl["target"] for fl in state.flags)
        corrected = any("mis-categorised" in f.statement and f"corrected category: {p['correct_category']}" in
                        " ".join(f.audit_notes) for f in state.findings)
        return vendor_flagged and corrected
    if t == "scanned_pdf":
        inv = next((i for i in state.invoices if _norm(i["path"]) == _norm(p["file"])), None)
        return bool(inv and abs(inv["line_sum"] - p["amount"]) <= 0.01 * p["amount"])
    if t == "corrupt_file":
        return any(_norm(n["input"]) == _norm(p["file"]) for n in state.not_analysed)
    if t == "duplicate":
        said = [fl["issue"] + " " + str(fl["target"]) for fl in state.flags] + [f.statement for f in state.findings]
        return any("duplicate" in s.lower() and p["number"] in s for s in said)
    if t == "fixture":
        return any(f.status in ("overturned", "downgraded") and f.category == p["category"] for f in state.findings)
    return False


def _unsupported_numbers(report: str) -> int:
    """Rows of the Findings table that contain a number but cite no source."""
    rows = report.split("## Findings", 1)[-1].split("##", 1)[0].splitlines()
    return sum(1 for r in rows if r.startswith("| ") and not r.startswith("| Area") and re.search(r"\d", r)
               and not re.search(r"\[\d+\]", r) and "Internal" not in r and "Infra" not in r)


def score_run(run_id: str) -> dict:
    state = RunState.model_validate_json(Path(f"runs/{run_id}/state.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    truth_path = truth_for(state.input_dir)
    truth = json.loads(truth_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    report_path = Path(f"runs/{run_id}/report.md")
    report = report_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if report_path.exists() else ""
    everything = [p for p in truth["planted_errors"] if p]
    planted = [p for p in everything if p["type"] != "negative_control"]
    if state.data_mode == "fixture":  # fixture errors only count for runs that read fixtures
        planted += truth.get("fixtures", [])
    caught = {p["id"]: _caught(state, p, truth) for p in planted}
    false_alarms = _false_alarms(state, planted)
    errs = {}
    for cat, true_cost in truth["people_cost_fy27"].items():
        got = state.budget.get("people_cost", {}).get(cat)
        errs[cat] = None if got is None else round(100 * abs(got - true_cost) / true_cost, 3)
    inv_true = truth["invoice_totals_by_true_category"]
    inv_got: dict[str, float] = {}
    for inv in state.invoices:
        if inv.get("duplicate_of"):  # a re-sent invoice is not new spend
            continue
        inv_got[inv["category"]] = inv_got.get(inv["category"], 0) + inv["line_sum"]
    inv_err = {c: round(100 * abs(inv_got.get(c, 0) - v) / v, 2) for c, v in inv_true.items()}
    usage = {m: u for m, u in state.llm_usage.items()}
    return {
        "run_id": run_id, "trace_id": state.trace_id, "git_sha": state.git_sha, "tags": state.tags,
        "phase": state.phase, "data_mode": state.data_mode, "injected": state.injected,
        "dataset": Path(state.input_dir).name, "ground_truth": truth_path.as_posix(),
        "planted_caught": sum(caught.values()), "planted_total": len(caught), "planted_detail": caught,
        "false_alarms": len(false_alarms), "false_alarm_detail": false_alarms,
        "people_cost_abs_pct_error": errs,
        "invoice_category_abs_pct_error": inv_err,
        "unsupported_numbers_in_report": _unsupported_numbers(report),
        "findings": {f.id: {"status": f.status, "confidence": f.confidence} for f in state.findings},
        "overturned": sum(f.status == "overturned" for f in state.findings),
        "downgraded": sum(f.status == "downgraded" for f in state.findings),
        "recovery_decisions": len(state.decisions),
        "recovery_non_default": sum(d.chosen != d.default for d in state.decisions),
        "llm_calls": sum(u["calls"] for u in usage.values()),
        "llm_tokens_in": sum(u["tokens_in"] for u in usage.values()),
        "llm_tokens_out": sum(u["tokens_out"] for u in usage.values()),
        "llm_latency_s": round(sum(u["latency_s"] for u in usage.values()), 1),
        "fallback_hops": sum(u.get("fallback_hops", 0) for u in usage.values()),
        "provider_mix": sorted(usage), "llm_usage": usage,
        "crustdata_credits": state.crustdata_credits,
    }


def _agg(vals: list[float]) -> dict:
    return {"mean": round(statistics.mean(vals), 3), "min": min(vals), "max": max(vals), "n": len(vals)}


def run_eval(n: int, variant: str, evidence: bool, score_only: list[str] | None = None,
             fixtures: str | None = None, data: str = "data/acme") -> Path:
    run_ids = list(score_only or [])
    for _ in range(0 if score_only else n):
        cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "spendradar", "run", data, "--variant", variant]
        cmd += ["--evidence"] if evidence else []
        cmd += ["--fixtures", fixtures] if fixtures else []
        out = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
        m = re.search(r'"run_id": "([^"]+)"', out.stdout)
        if not m:
            print(out.stdout[-2000:], out.stderr[-2000:])
            raise SystemExit("run failed to start")
        run_ids.append(m.group(1))
    scores = [score_run(r) for r in run_ids]
    no_fallback = [s for s in scores if s["fallback_hops"] == 0]
    keys = ("planted_caught", "false_alarms", "unsupported_numbers_in_report", "overturned", "downgraded", "recovery_decisions",
            "llm_calls", "llm_tokens_in", "llm_tokens_out", "llm_latency_s", "crustdata_credits")
    card = {
        "created": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"), "variant": variant, "evidence": evidence,
        "git_sha": scores[0]["git_sha"] if scores else "", "n_runs": len(scores),
        "n_runs_without_fallback": len(no_fallback),
        "planted_total": scores[0]["planted_total"] if scores else 0,
        "summary_all_runs": {k: _agg([s[k] for s in scores]) for k in keys} if scores else {},
        "summary_no_fallback_runs": {k: _agg([s[k] for s in no_fallback]) for k in keys} if no_fallback else {},
        "runs": scores,
    }
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = OUT / f"{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%S')}-{card['git_sha']}-{variant}.json"
    path.write_text(json.dumps(card, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    return path

def _evidence_against(state: RunState, f: Finding, news: list[dict]) -> list[str]:
    ev = []
    if f.kind == "policy":
        for p in state.competitors.values():
            r = analysis.category_range(p, f.category)
            if not r:
                continue
            sigs = [s for s in p.signals if s.category == f.category]
            ag = analysis.signal_agreement(p, f.category)
            if ag is not None and ag < 0.6:
                ev.append(f"{p.name} {f.category} signals disagree: " + "; ".join(
                    f"{s.name}={s.headcount:.0f} (as of {s.as_of})" for s in sigs))
        for n in news:
            ev.append(f"news {n['date']} {n['company']}: {n['title']} ({n['url']})")
    if "mis-categorised" in f.statement:
        vendor = f.statement.split(":")[0]
        for inv in state.invoices:
            if inv["vendor"] == vendor:
                ev.append(f"{inv['number']} cost centre '{inv['cost_centre']}' → {inv['category']}; lines: "
                          + "; ".join(line['description'] for line in inv["lines"]))
    return ev


def _judge(role: str, f: Finding, evidence: list[str], checks: list[str],
           exclude: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> tuple[Verdict, llm.LLMResult]:
    prompt = (f"FINDING ({f.category}, confidence {f.confidence}):\n{f.statement}\n\n"
              f"DETERMINISTIC CHECKS:\n" + "\n".join(f"- {c}" for c in checks)
              + "\n\nEVIDENCE THAT MIGHT CONTRADICT IT:\n" + ("\n".join(f"- {e}" for e in evidence) or "- none found")
              + "\n\nTry to disprove the finding. 'overturn' = the evidence shows it is wrong or unsupported; "
                "'downgrade' = it may hold but the evidence weakens it materially; 'confirm' = it survives. "
                "For an invoice flagged as mis-categorised, decide from the LINE ITEMS: does the work belong to the "
                "category of the cost centre it was billed to? The kind of work decides the category, not which "
                "cost centre paid. If any invoice's line items do not match its cost centre, the flag is correct: "
                "'confirm' and set corrected_category to the category the line items belong to. "
                "Judge only from the evidence given; do not invent facts.")
    res = llm.complete(role, prompt, schema=Verdict, exclude=exclude,
                       system="You are a sceptical finance auditor checking an analyst's findings.")
    return res.parsed, res


def self_audit(state: RunState) -> None:
    news = _recent_negative_news(state)
    second_left = llm.CONFIG["second_opinion_max_per_run"]
    for f in state.findings:
        with neatlogs.trace(f"audit:{f.id}", kind="AGENT") as span:
            rc_ok, rc = _recompute_ok(state, f)
            src_ok, src = _sources_ok(state, f)
            evidence = _evidence_against(state, f, news)
            checks = [rc, src]
            span.set_attribute("spendradar.audit.evidence", json.dumps(evidence)[:2000])
            set_io(span, input={"finding": f.id, "statement": f.statement, "evidence_against": evidence})
            if not rc_ok or not src_ok:
                f.status, f.audit_notes = "overturned", [rc, src]
                span.set_attribute("spendradar.audit.verdict", "overturned (deterministic)")
                set_io(span, output={"status": f.status, "how": "deterministic", "notes": f.audit_notes})
                continue
            if not evidence and f.kind == "internal" and "mis-categorised" not in f.statement:
                f.status = "confirmed"
                f.audit_notes.append("deterministic internal finding; no contradicting evidence")
                span.set_attribute("spendradar.audit.verdict", "confirmed (deterministic)")
                set_io(span, output={"status": f.status, "how": "deterministic", "notes": f.audit_notes})
                continue
            try:
                v, res = _judge("reason", f, evidence, checks)
                _usage_add(state, res)
            except llm.LLMError as e:
                f.status = "downgraded"
                f.audit_notes.append(f"audit LLM unavailable ({str(e)[:80]}); downgraded to be safe")
                set_io(span, output={"status": f.status, "how": "llm unavailable", "notes": f.audit_notes})
                continue
            f.audit_notes.append(f"{res.model}: {v.verdict} — {v.reason}")
            final = v.verdict
            if v.verdict != "confirm" and second_left > 0:
                second_left -= 1
                try:
                    # Independent means a different model from the verdict being checked.
                    v2, res2 = _judge("second_opinion", f, evidence, checks, exclude=(res.model,))
                    _usage_add(state, res2)
                    f.audit_notes.append(f"second opinion {res2.model}: {v2.verdict} — {v2.reason}")
                    span.set_attribute("spendradar.audit.second_opinion", v2.verdict)
                    if v2.verdict == "confirm" and v.verdict == "overturn":
                        final = "downgrade"  # disagreement between providers → soften, never silently confirm
                except llm.LLMError as e:
                    f.audit_notes.append(f"second opinion unavailable: {str(e)[:80]}")
            f.status = {"confirm": "confirmed", "downgrade": "downgraded", "overturn": "overturned"}[final]
            if final != "confirm":
                f.confidence = round(f.confidence * (0.5 if final == "downgrade" else 0.0), 3)
            if "mis-categorised" in f.statement and v.corrected_category != "none":
                f.audit_notes.append(f"corrected category: {v.corrected_category}")
                f.status = "confirmed"  # the flag itself is confirmed; the correction is applied in the report
                f.confidence = 1.0 if v.verdict != "overturn" else f.confidence
            span.set_attribute("spendradar.audit.verdict", f.status)
            set_io(span, output={"status": f.status, "how": "llm", "confidence": f.confidence, "notes": f.audit_notes})

"""Self-audit: try to disprove every finding before it reaches the report.

Per finding:
  1. recompute   — rerun the deterministic comparison from stored state; numbers must match
  2. sources     — every figure the finding uses must exist and carry a source
  3. contradict  — look for evidence against it (signal disagreement, layoff/freeze news for a
                   competitor in the median, vendor billed to two categories) and let the LLM judge
  4. second opinion — an independent OpenRouter :free model re-judges findings Gemini marked
                   downgrade/overturn (advisory, max N per run)
Findings that fail are downgraded or overturned and listed with both sides of the evidence.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from datetime import date, datetime
from typing import Literal

import neatlogs
from pydantic import BaseModel

from spendradar import analysis, llm
from spendradar.tracing import set_io
from spendradar.models import Finding, RunState

NEWS_WORDS = ("layoff", "lay off", "laid off", "job cuts", "cuts jobs", "restructur", "hiring freeze",
              "downsiz", "reduction in force", "acquired by", "acquisition of")
NEWS_WINDOW_DAYS = 180


class Verdict(BaseModel):
    verdict: Literal["confirm", "downgrade", "overturn"]
    reason: str
    corrected_category: Literal["engineering", "ml_ai", "sales", "marketing", "infra_cloud", "none"] = "none"


def _recent_negative_news(state: RunState) -> list[dict]:
    hits = []
    for p in state.competitors.values():
        for n in p.news:
            title = (n.get("title") or "").lower()
            try:
                age = (date.today() - datetime.fromisoformat(n["date"][:10]).date()).days
            except Exception:
                continue
            if age <= NEWS_WINDOW_DAYS and any(w in title for w in NEWS_WORDS):
                hits.append({"company": p.name, **n})
    return hits


def _recompute_ok(state: RunState, f: Finding) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    if f.kind != "policy":
        return True, "internal finding: deterministic"
    rule = next((r for r in state.policy.get("rules", []) if r["category"] == f.category), None)
    ours = analysis.our_position(state.budget)
    res = analysis.compare({**ours[f.category], "_total": ours["_total"]},
                           analysis.competitor_shares(list(state.competitors.values()), f.category),
                           rule, state.salary.get(f.category, 0))
    ok = (res.get("status") == "ok" and abs(res["median_low"] - (f.theirs_low or 0)) < 1e-9
          and abs(res["median_high"] - (f.theirs_high or 0)) < 1e-9 and res["violated"] == f.policy_violated)
    return ok, "recomputed and matched" if ok else f"recompute mismatch: {res}"


def _sources_ok(state: RunState, f: Finding) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    missing = [fid for fid in f.figure_ids if fid not in state.figures or not state.figures[fid].sources]
    return not missing, "all figures sourced" if not missing else f"unsourced figures: {missing}"


def _evidence_against(state: RunState, f: Finding, news: list[dict]) -> list[str]:
    ev = []
    if f.kind == "policy":
        for p in state.competitors.values():
            r = analysis.category_range(p, f.category)
            if not r:
                continue
            sigs = [s for s in p.signals if s.category == f.category]
            ag = analysis.signal_agreement(p, f.category)
            if ag is not None and ag < 0.6:
                ev.append(f"{p.name} {f.category} signals disagree: " + "; ".join(
                    f"{s.name}={s.headcount:.0f} (as of {s.as_of})" for s in sigs))
        for n in news:
            ev.append(f"news {n['date']} {n['company']}: {n['title']} ({n['url']})")
    if "mis-categorised" in f.statement:
        vendor = f.statement.split(":")[0]
        for inv in state.invoices:
            if inv["vendor"] == vendor:
                ev.append(f"{inv['number']} cost centre '{inv['cost_centre']}' → {inv['category']}; lines: "
                          + "; ".join(line['description'] for line in inv["lines"]))
    return ev


def _judge(role: str, f: Finding, evidence: list[str], checks: list[str],
           exclude: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> tuple[Verdict, llm.LLMResult]:
    prompt = (f"FINDING ({f.category}, confidence {f.confidence}):\n{f.statement}\n\n"
              f"DETERMINISTIC CHECKS:\n" + "\n".join(f"- {c}" for c in checks)
              + "\n\nEVIDENCE THAT MIGHT CONTRADICT IT:\n" + ("\n".join(f"- {e}" for e in evidence) or "- none found")
              + "\n\nTry to disprove the finding. 'overturn' = the evidence shows it is wrong or unsupported; "
                "'downgrade' = it may hold but the evidence weakens it materially; 'confirm' = it survives. "
                "For an invoice flagged as mis-categorised, decide from the LINE ITEMS: does the work belong to the "
                "category of the cost centre it was billed to? The kind of work decides the category, not which "
                "cost centre paid. If any invoice's line items do not match its cost centre, the flag is correct: "
                "'confirm' and set corrected_category to the category the line items belong to. "
                "Judge only from the evidence given; do not invent facts.")
    res = llm.complete(role, prompt, schema=Verdict, exclude=exclude,
                       system="You are a sceptical finance auditor checking an analyst's findings.")
    return res.parsed, res


def self_audit(state: RunState) -> None:
    news = _recent_negative_news(state)
    second_left = llm.CONFIG["second_opinion_max_per_run"]
    for f in state.findings:
        with neatlogs.trace(f"audit:{f.id}", kind="AGENT") as span:
            rc_ok, rc = _recompute_ok(state, f)
            src_ok, src = _sources_ok(state, f)
            evidence = _evidence_against(state, f, news)
            checks = [rc, src]
            span.set_attribute("spendradar.audit.evidence", json.dumps(evidence)[:2000])
            set_io(span, input={"finding": f.id, "statement": f.statement, "evidence_against": evidence})
            if not rc_ok or not src_ok:
                f.status, f.audit_notes = "overturned", [rc, src]
                span.set_attribute("spendradar.audit.verdict", "overturned (deterministic)")
                set_io(span, output={"status": f.status, "how": "deterministic", "notes": f.audit_notes})
                continue
            if not evidence and f.kind == "internal" and "mis-categorised" not in f.statement:
                f.status = "confirmed"
                f.audit_notes.append("deterministic internal finding; no contradicting evidence")
                span.set_attribute("spendradar.audit.verdict", "confirmed (deterministic)")
                set_io(span, output={"status": f.status, "how": "deterministic", "notes": f.audit_notes})
                continue
            try:
                v, res = _judge("reason", f, evidence, checks)
                _usage_add(state, res)
            except llm.LLMError as e:
                f.status = "downgraded"
                f.audit_notes.append(f"audit LLM unavailable ({str(e)[:80]}); downgraded to be safe")
                set_io(span, output={"status": f.status, "how": "llm unavailable", "notes": f.audit_notes})
                continue
            f.audit_notes.append(f"{res.model}: {v.verdict} — {v.reason}")
            final = v.verdict
            if v.verdict != "confirm" and second_left > 0:
                second_left -= 1
                try:
                    # Independent means a different model from the verdict being checked.
                    v2, res2 = _judge("second_opinion", f, evidence, checks, exclude=(res.model,))
                    _usage_add(state, res2)
                    f.audit_notes.append(f"second opinion {res2.model}: {v2.verdict} — {v2.reason}")
                    span.set_attribute("spendradar.audit.second_opinion", v2.verdict)
                    if v2.verdict == "confirm" and v.verdict == "overturn":
                        final = "downgrade"  # disagreement between providers → soften, never silently confirm
                except llm.LLMError as e:
                    f.audit_notes.append(f"second opinion unavailable: {str(e)[:80]}")
            f.status = {"confirm": "confirmed", "downgrade": "downgraded", "overturn": "overturned"}[final]
            if final != "confirm":
                f.confidence = round(f.confidence * (0.5 if final == "downgrade" else 0.0), 3)
            if "mis-categorised" in f.statement and v.corrected_category != "none":
                f.audit_notes.append(f"corrected category: {v.corrected_category}")
                f.status = "confirmed"  # the flag itself is confirmed; the correction is applied in the report
                f.confidence = 1.0 if v.verdict != "overturn" else f.confidence
            span.set_attribute("spendradar.audit.verdict", f.status)
            set_io(span, output={"status": f.status, "how": "llm", "confidence": f.confidence, "notes": f.audit_notes})


def _usage_add(state: RunState, res: llm.LLMResult) -> None:
    from spendradar.agent import _usage

    _usage(state, res)
